pathophysiology.summary: Hormonal treatment (for example the combined oral contraceptive pill or a progestogen) is offered and has no permanent negative effect on subsequent fertility. For deep endometriosis involving the bowel, bladder or ureter, 3 months of a GnRH agonist before surgery can be considered. Surgery should be laparoscopic unless contraindicated; at hysterectomy all visible lesions should be excised. Hormonal treatment is not offered alone or with surgery to improve fertility.

clinicalManagement.title: Analgesia
actions: Short trial of paracetamol or an NSAID; if ineffective consider other pain management and referral.

clinicalManagement.title: Hormonal treatment
actions: Offer the combined oral contraceptive pill or a progestogen; explain no permanent effect on fertility.

clinicalManagement.title: Surgery
actions: Laparoscopic surgery; GnRH agonist for 3 months before surgery in deep disease; consider hormonal treatment after surgery.

clinicalManagement.title: Fertility
actions: Do not offer hormonal treatment for fertility; offer excision or ablation with adhesiolysis for disease not involving bowel, bladder or ureter; multidisciplinary fertility input.

clinicalManagement.title: Follow-up
actions: Consider outpatient follow-up for deep disease or endometrioma larger than 3 cm.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG73 names paracetamol or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, the combined oral contraceptive pill or a progestogen, and a GnRH agonist for 3 months before surgery (off-label as of September 2017) but gives no doses and no add-back regimen. Follow product information and local protocol. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
